title: Security of quantum key distribution with passive basis choice and detection-efficiency mismatch for a realistic satellite setup
authors: Egor Ivchenko, Aleksandr Khmelev, Vladimir Kurochkin, Anton Trushechkin
abstract: Detection-efficiency mismatch is a common problem in realistic quantum key distribution (QKD) systems. The existing security proofs for the case of the passive basis choice provide a nonzero secret key rate only for a small detection-efficiency mismatch. Unfortunately, in realistic setups, the detection-efficiency mismatch can be significant. Here we present a more precise estimation of the secret key rate for the BB84 protocol with the passive basis choice, which accounts for the detection-efficiency mismatch between four threshold detectors as well as an adaptation of the decoy-state method. The suggested approach is used to estimate the secret key rate in a QKD experiment between the Micius satellite and the Zvenigorod ground station.
summary: This paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis of the secret key rate for QKD over satellite links, specifically addressing the failure of existing security proofs when detector efficiencies mismatch significantly. By employing advanced information theoretic techniques and adapting the decoy-state method, the authors derive more precise bounds necessary for assessing practical quantum communication security.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the secret key rate for Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) when significant detection-efficiency mismatch occurs in realistic satellite communication setups.
main_result: The authors develop a rigorous framework to estimate the key rate under large mismatches, showing that existing proofs fail and providing updated bounds based on information theory optimization techniques.
method: The analysis employs Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs) and adapts the decoy-state method within the BB84 protocol framework. Key rates are derived by solving complex optimization problems involving conditional entropies.
model_or_system: The model simulates a satellite-to-ground QKD link, specifically between the Micius satellite and the Zvenigorod ground station. It utilizes the BB84 protocol considering single-photon states and weak coherent pulses.
key_observables: Secret key rate ($K$), conditional von-Neumann entropies, Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), and detection efficiencies ($\eta_{a,\alpha}$).
important_parameters: Detection-efficiency mismatch magnitude, probability of passing ($p_{	ext{pass}}$), and the average photon number ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an asymptotic limit ($N ightarrow \infty$) and that Eve knows the exact detection efficiency values but cannot manipulate them.

paper_structure: The paper builds from general security proofs to specific estimations using POVMs and decoy states. It presents multiple key rate bounds derived through optimization over symmetry-enforcing linear maps, culminating in an estimate applicable to the Micius satellite link.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles a critical practical limitation (detector mismatch) in quantum communication theory, providing necessary theoretical tools for assessing real-world quantum network security.
